newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deadline for German refinery sale moved to mid-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Deadline for German refinery sale moved to mid-Feb.

text.p: The deadline for the sale of Germany's bankrupt BETA refinery in Wilhelmshaven has been moved from the end of January to the middle of February, managing director Hans Van Weelden said on Thursday.
"We are still negotiating the contracts, I expect the transaction will be successfully completed by mid-February," he said.
The offers received looked promising and a new owner would be found.
But he would not comment on which of the two competing bidders -- SA Louis Dreyfus CIE or Bulk Oil AG of Switzerland -- practically the former co-owners, was likely to be chosen.
The 190,000 barrel per day refinery went into receivership last year as a result of a long-standing dispute between Dreyfus and Holding Tusculum BV.
Sources familiar with the companies have said Bulk Oil AG has the same majority shareholders as Tusculum.
Crude oil processing at the refinery has been extended until April 3, 1997.
